topicName: Sprint Backlog: Commitment and Execution Plan
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Sprint Backlog: Commitment and Execution Plan in Scrum"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Sprint Backlog is a highly visible, real-time picture of the work that the Development Team plans to accomplish during the upcoming Sprint. It serves as both a commitment to the Product Owner regarding what value will be delivered and an execution plan for how that value will be achieved."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Core Components of the Sprint Backlog"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"The Sprint Goal: A concise objective for the Sprint, agreed upon during the Sprint Planning meeting."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Selected Product Backlog Items: A set of user stories or features pulled from the Product Backlog."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"The Execution Plan: A breakdown of the selected Product Backlog items into actionable, technical tasks (typically ranging from 4 to 16 hours of work)."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating the Execution Plan"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"During Sprint Planning, the team decomposes user stories into granular tasks. This ensures every team member understands the implementation details, technical dependencies, and acceptance criteria. Below is an example structure of how a backlog item is broken down into an execution task list."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"User Story: US-102 - Implement User Authentication
Task 1: Design database schema for users (4 hrs)
Task 2: Setup JWT authentication endpoints (6 hrs)
Task 3: Build frontend login form component (8 hrs)
Task 4: Write unit and integration tests (4 hrs)"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Managing and Updating the Sprint Backlog"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Sprint Backlog is a living artifact. Throughout the Sprint, the Development Team updates the backlog as they learn more about the work required. If a task takes longer than expected, or if a new technical dependency is discovered, the remaining work is recalculated daily."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Daily Adaptation: Inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal during the Daily Scrum and adjust the Sprint Backlog tasks as needed."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Ownership: Only the Development Team can modify the Sprint Backlog during the Sprint. It belongs to them."},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"A well-maintained Sprint Backlog bridges the gap between high-level product vision and daily engineering execution. By treating it as a dynamic plan rather than a rigid contract, teams can maximize adaptability while honoring their commitment to the Sprint Goal."}]
